ops.title: Native Codex TUI and Orca terminal smoke
ops.body:
The frozen cc-codex candidate SHA-256 2eaaca83896b3265c70b5763a7608b199aa3c5f0c14c1ed144a0fc8b2076cb23 launched the native Codex 0.155.1 TUI in a Terminal Control PTY. A fresh native thread returned ORDINARY_NATIVE_ACK, exposed a real read-only-sandbox approval for touch approval-probe.txt, accepted one-time approval, created the file, and returned APPROVAL_NATIVE_ACK.

The same persisted thread resumed in Orca terminal term_785a0b15-c919-49b7-b7b5-89e624671054. Its prior transcript was visible, Orca observed input_accepted and turn_started for a new prompt, the model returned ORCA_RESUME_ACK, the binding advanced to generation 2, and a manual startup-notification wrapper restored the exact Orca terminal context plus the authoritative Codex thread and account identity.

Known limits and finding: native remote resume rejects permission overrides, so the successful resume omitted them; pre-binding notification replay and graphical notifications were not exercised; no desktop client was started. The frozen candidate stored ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN and ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_ENDPOINT in terminal_env without exposing their values here, confirming the separately assigned broad-routing-prefix review finding. Full evidence and cleanup details are attached from /tmp/codex-port-terminal-smoke.txt.
